one_line: Shared AI-assisted fashion storefront for intent-based shopping.
what_it_does: Lets a shopper browse live products while an agent searches, checks size, reviews, prices, and fills the bag using shared session state.
leverage_rationale: Typed commerce tools and shared shopper signals make intent search, size/price checking, and agent-human co-browsing substantially more reliable than coordinate-driven UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes live shared catalog and bag session.
Tools cover search, sizes, reviews, price tracking, and shopper signals.
Fashion catalog and agent-side workflow are visible in video evidence.
execution_rationale: The storefront, catalog, product detail, and shared shopping flow appear coherent and intentionally packaged, with strong visual continuity and a live demo.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion frame sheets show catalog and shopping interfaces.
Devpost packaging shows a branded fashion storefront demo.
impact_rationale: Online shoppers have a concrete discovery and decision-friction problem; preserving visual browsing while delegating tedious checks is credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific fashion-shopping scenario and constraints are described.
Visible product catalog and shopping flow.
creativity_rationale: Combines agentic filtering with human visual discovery rather than reducing shopping to a chatbot recommendation.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent shop together in the same live storefront.
Concept explicitly preserves browsing and discovery.
usability_note: Clear storefront metaphor and shared interaction; complexity of agent controls is not fully observable.
advance_reason: High-quality, clearly WebMCP-centered commerce workflow with credible user value.

one_line: Shared semantic mystery board for human-agent evidence reasoning.
what_it_does: Provides a visual corkboard where people and agents pin, connect, inspect, search, audit, and propose relationships among clues.
leverage_rationale: Structured evidence IDs, directional relations, provenance, proposal status, and semantic regions expose board meaning that a general agent could not reliably recover from pixels.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies 22 typed tools over cases, cards, relations, trash, viewport, and undo.
Agent proposals remain visible and provisional on the shared board.
Video shows the shared mystery-board product workflow.
execution_rationale: The concept, visual board, provenance model, and human review boundary form a coherent and unusually complete workflow for the stated scope.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets consistently show the board interface and clue organization.
Packaging presents inspectable, auditable shared reasoning.
impact_rationale: Investigators, researchers, incident reviewers, and threat-modelers have real value in shared spatial evidence synthesis; the playful mystery is a credible demonstration.
impact_evidence: Description names research synthesis, incident review, threat modeling, debugging, reporting, and risk analysis.
Visible board supports evidence-oriented work.
creativity_rationale: The spatial corkboard is a memorable interaction model that preserves human visual reasoning while adding semantic agent operations and provenance.
creativity_evidence: Human-agent shared mystery board.
Typed directional deductions with rationale, confidence, and provenance.
usability_note: Tactile board metaphor is legible, though dense evidence graphs may require learning.
advance_reason: One of the clearest examples of WebMCP changing the interaction model itself.

one_line: Privacy-preserving personalized apparel shopping through the user’s agent.
what_it_does: Lets an external agent use private fit and household context to search apparel, compare variants, assemble looks, and shop without the retailer storing the profile.
leverage_rationale: Semantic commerce tools let a user-side agent apply private constraints directly to retailer product data, avoiding repeated manual entry and DOM automation.
leverage_evidence: Zero-knowledge design keeps profile context with the user agent.
Tools include search, matching variants, size guide, cart, and proposal operations.
Video shows a substantial apparel storefront workflow.
execution_rationale: The retail experience is coherent and the privacy/agent boundary is consistently articulated, with a working-looking catalog and demo flow.
execution_evidence: Three video sheets show apparel catalog and shopping states.
Devpost packaging shows a detailed retail interface.
impact_rationale: Shoppers who dislike repetitive sizing and family shopping can gain meaningful convenience without surrendering sensitive measurements to each retailer.
impact_evidence: Concrete Hawaii family-outfit scenario.
Product supports multiple people and missing-item discovery.
creativity_rationale: The combination of user-held personal context and retailer-held product knowledge is a fresh, coherent privacy-centered shopping model.
creativity_evidence: Retailer need not know the user’s profile.
Agent knows fit while the site exposes product semantics.
usability_note: Familiar storefront reduces friction; privacy and agent attachment mechanics may be unfamiliar.
standouts: Strong privacy architecture for agentic commerce.
advance_reason: Meaningful WebMCP leverage with a concrete, differentiated commerce use case.

one_line: Teach catalog classification rules by example with safe preview branches.
what_it_does: Turns a human product edit into agent proposals for related catalog items, supports corrections and revisions, and keeps merge under human control.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes exact human activity, product state, branch proposals, corrections, and diffs so the agent can generalize from demonstrations without unsafe direct edits.
leverage_evidence: ShowOnce + BranchMode workflow is explicitly tool-mediated.
Current-versus-preview diff and human-controlled merge are visible.
Tools read activity, create branches, revise proposals, and inspect diffs.
execution_rationale: The central workflow is unusually well specified end to end: demonstrate, preview, correct, revise, review, and merge.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets show form, proposal, and table/diff states.
Description reports 10 proposals and 20 changed fields in an isolated preview.
impact_rationale: Catalog operators face repetitive, error-prone classification work; safe generalization with review directly addresses that problem.
impact_evidence: Specific catalog-operations audience and repetitive task.
Preview and correction workflow addresses error risk.
creativity_rationale: Teaching rules through a single real edit plus iterative correction is a strong original interaction model for agent-assisted operations.
creativity_evidence: Human demonstration becomes an isolated branch rather than a prompt.
Corrections feed revision while preserving merge authority.
usability_note: Preview/diff control is understandable; branch concepts add operational complexity.
standouts: Strong end-to-end evidence and control boundary.
advance_reason: Top-tier WebMCP-native workflow with strong execution evidence and originality.

one_line: SRE incident workbench with agent investigation and operator-approved mitigation.
what_it_does: Combines incident telemetry, logs, deployment comparison, diagnostics, staged rollback, approval, execution, recovery, and postmortem drafting.
leverage_rationale: Typed incident tools make investigation and mitigation staging precise and replayable, while the UI-only approval boundary gives the agent structured context without granting unsafe execution.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools cover detect-to-recover workflow.
Execution revalidates incident phase, mitigation IDs, approval source, and replay protection.
Video consistently shows an operational incident dashboard.
execution_rationale: The simulated regression, evidence timeline, staged rollback, approval gate, recovery metrics, and postmortem form a coherent complete scope.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show consistent multi-panel SRE dashboard states.
Description gives concrete before/after latency and error metrics and full flow.
impact_rationale: Incident response is a high-value operational problem; accountable agent investigation and safer mitigation staging directly benefit SRE teams.
impact_evidence: Specific checkout-api regression scenario.
Operator approval and blast-radius review address real production risk.
creativity_rationale: The explicit distinction between autonomous investigation and human-authorized execution is a thoughtful, memorable agent-native SRE pattern.
creativity_evidence: No approval tool; visible UI is the authority.
Recovery and replay protection are part of the product model.
usability_note: Operational dashboard is information-dense but organized around a familiar incident lifecycle.
standouts: Concrete incident lifecycle and recovery evidence.
advance_reason: Highly credible SRE use case with strong execution and safety design.

one_line: Policy enforcement layer that constrains and authorizes agent actions.
what_it_does: Stores human purchasing boundaries, validates agent proposals, blocks violations, requests additional authority, and requires human confirmation before one-time execution.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP handlers act as deterministic enforcement points between agent intent and side effects; a general UI-driving agent cannot provide the same reliable policy boundary.
leverage_evidence: Five tools implement mission, proposal, authorization, and commit stages.
ALLOW, BLOCK, and UNDETERMINED outcomes include exact reasons.
Mission versions, expiring tokens, and execute-once protection are described.
execution_rationale: The authorization workflow and safety states are coherent and strongly packaged, though the video is more demonstrative than deeply end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show security/blocked/live-demo states.
Description reports automated tests and prepare-confirm-commit workflow.
impact_rationale: Users need enforceable boundaries when agents can make consequential purchases or changes; explicit policy and confirmation provide direct safety value.
impact_evidence: Concrete maximum-total, quantity, delivery, and vendor rules.
Blocked webpage-induced deviations are explained to the user.
creativity_rationale: Treating site-side WebMCP handlers as authorization and intent-integrity boundaries is a strong, timely interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Website verifies agent proposals rather than trusting agent-supplied approval.
Permission changes remain human-controlled.
usability_note: Clear ALLOW/BLOCK outcomes; handling UNDETERMINED and permission escalation may add friction.
red_flags: Video packaging is partly promotional and does not expose every enforcement transition.
standouts: Deterministic policy enforcement at the website boundary.
advance_reason: A high-leverage safety primitive with a clear real-world need.

one_line: Safe agent-operated WordPress editing with staged drafts, approval, and rollback.
what_it_does: Exposes WordPress page, SEO, readability, and WooCommerce operations as WebMCP tools while staging changes for same-page human review and rollback.
leverage_rationale: Agent-only draft/approve/reject and rollback operations create a structured safe write path across WordPress capabilities rather than brittle UI clicking.
leverage_evidence: Description reports curated site tools, staged duplicate previews, approval/rejection, audit, and rollback.
319-tool bridge maps WordPress abilities to WebMCP.
Video shows WordPress editing/demo states.
execution_rationale: The integration target, permission model, draft workflow, and rollback story are coherent and supported by a substantial demo/package.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show site-editing and preview-oriented product motion.
Devpost shows a WordPress-specific live demo and concrete integration architecture.
impact_rationale: WordPress owners and agencies have frequent content and catalog maintenance needs; safe agent-assisted editing with review and rollback is directly useful.
impact_evidence: Supports pages, SEO/readability, and WooCommerce gaps.
Human approval and rollback address the main risk of agent writes.
creativity_rationale: Putting an agent’s safe write path directly on the page, with preview links and approval, is a useful and well-developed integration pattern.
creativity_evidence: Approve-duplicate and reject-duplicate are meaningful as site tools.
Works through WordPress abilities and per-tool permissions.
usability_note: Familiar WordPress target, but login and large tool surface may complicate setup.
red_flags: Claims broad compatibility across page builders are not fully verifiable from packet evidence.
standouts: Draft, approval, and rollback safety loop.
advance_reason: Strong practical integration with meaningful agent-write safety controls.

leverage_rationale: The shared live state, durable household operations, receipts, and undo give agents a structured way to capture and retrieve ephemeral family knowledge beyond ordinary UI automation.

Durable Object owns operations and shared updates.
Video shows the house-based memory interface and populated states.
execution_rationale: The cutaway-house metaphor, room-linked memories, care circle, receipts, and live shared state form a coherent product with meaningful scope.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show consistent house/memory product presentation.
Description specifies shared updates and undo receipts.
impact_rationale: Households and caregivers have a real knowledge-loss and coordination problem; reducing capture friction and sharing care tasks can create substantial value even for a niche audience.
impact_evidence: Concrete examples include home maintenance and cardiology rides.
Targets family memory and caregiver coordination.
creativity_rationale: Representing household knowledge as a living cutaway home with room-based memories is memorable, emotionally resonant, and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: One shared illustrated house maps rooms, people, lamps, and memories.
Family agents participate in the same artifact.
usability_note: The house metaphor is inviting and lowers the abstraction of a family knowledge base.
standouts: Addresses caregiver coordination without reducing it to a task list.
advance_reason: High impact and creativity with a coherent shared-state product concept.

leverage_rationale: Structured playtest context, regex/variable patches, scenario comparison, and trigger bookkeeping solve state-tracking work that a general UI-driving agent would handle unreliably.
leverage_evidence: Ten tools separate deterministic page bookkeeping from agent judgment.
QA records misses, untriggered entries, warnings, and ordered tool calls.
Video shows document/table and testing-oriented interface states.
execution_rationale: The niche workflow is unusually specific and internally coherent, with creator and publisher modes and explicit QA outputs, though visible frames are text-dense.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show document/table panels and workflow views.
Description specifies checklist, playtest, transcript, QA, and comparison panels.
impact_rationale: SillyTavern creators and publishers have a real consistency and regression-testing problem; the audience is niche but the fit is strong.
impact_evidence: Specific character-card complexity and repeated QA burden are described.

creativity_rationale: Applying an agent-plus-deterministic-bookkeeping split to interactive character-card QA is a fresh, technically focused concept.

Compares final variable state across scenarios.

one_line: Wearability decision layer that can recommend buy, restyle, wait, or skip.
what_it_does: Scores apparel against occasion, budget, fit, timing, owned items, product facts, purchase risk, and rewear value, with cited verdicts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes live product facts and constraints for a decision layer that can explain and cite a no-buy verdict, rather than merely automating checkout.
leverage_evidence: Four verdicts include buy, restyle, wait, and skip.
Description cites live AJIO measurements, stock, fit distribution, and provenance.
Video shows the decision-oriented shopping interface.
execution_rationale: The product has a focused decision model, clear verdict semantics, and a coherent evidence/citation presentation, with a live shopping demo.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show branded shopping/decision workflow.
Description specifies four scoring axes and cited verdicts.
impact_rationale: Shoppers face overbuying, poor fit, occasion mismatch, and low rewear value; a transparent recommendation to wait or skip has credible value.
impact_evidence: Concrete occasion, budget, deadline, fit, and owned-wardrobe inputs.
Addresses the failure mode of optimizing only price and availability.
creativity_rationale: Making ‘don’t buy’ a first-class agent outcome and combining wearability with rewear value is a strong new angle on shopping agents.
creativity_evidence: Buy/restyle/wait/skip decision set.
Verdicts are cited to user inputs, product data, or rules.
usability_note: Decision labels are immediately understandable; detailed evidence may increase cognitive load.
red_flags: No public repository is listed, so eligibility is less certain than the other packets.
